clue.text: Toxic spirit around — close model plant

indicators.note: the toxic spirit's two words wrap round the next pair of pieces

parts.note: a shade is a ghost or spirit
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A poisonous ghost lurks close to a model plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts NIGH and T between DEADLY and SHADE, the two halves of the toxic spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Belladonna is a highly poisonous plant of the nightshade family.

clue.text: Sex splashed over morning papers

indicators.note: the shuffled word is spread over and around the morning abbreviation
splashed suggests the letters scattered about

explanation.surface: Tabloid sex stories splashed across the morning papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashed' rearranges SEX to EXS, and 'over' puts it round AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Exam papers are the written tests sat by students, so papers can stand for them.

clue.text: Furniture off-stage?

definitions.meaning: a sideboard with shelves for dishes
the theatre helper who dresses actors works off-stage

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture used off-stage.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a kitchen sideboard and the backstage assistant who helps actors change costume.

clue.text: The old sultanate, where this type of guard can be seen

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: A guard from an old Arabian sultanate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yeomen of the Guard are the British sovereign's bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yeomen of the Guard are a royal bodyguard, so the word names a kind of guard.

clue.text: Getting lit up with double gin and vermouth

indicators.note: up here means stirred about, so the letters are rearranged
double means the word gin is taken twice

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Getting drunk on double gin and vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' gives GINGIN, IT is added, and 'up' rearranges the lot; 'lit' also hints at drunkenness.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite is to set alight, so getting lit is catching fire.

clue.text: Figure he'll get cross, with no return on silver

parts.note: a cross is the letter X
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: return means the word no comes back the other way

explanation.surface: Someone is cross at getting no return on his silver investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns NO into ON, which sits on AG in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-sided plane shape is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Turn tables on men in this flawed ruling body

indicators.note: flawed suggests the words broken and remade in a new order

explanation.surface: An urge to turn the tables on the men in a flawed ruling body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flawed' rearranges TABLES, MEN and THIS together; 'Turn tables on' is idiomatic surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruling elite or governing class is known collectively as the establishment.

clue.text: Ring the bell and get a free admittance through it?

parts.note: to toll is to ring a bell

indicators.note: free suggests the letters let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Ring the bell and you get in free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges GET A into GATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier on a road where travellers pay a charge to pass, hence admittance through it.

clue.text: Catches a sheep breaking out —— after finding them?

indicators.note: breaking suggests the phrase smashed and reformed

explanation.surface: A flock escapes as a sheep breaks out of its pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges all thirteen letters of CATCHES A SHEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency exits in ships or aircraft are what you would get out through once found.

clue.text: See 1
Offensive manoeuvre by Sioux against poor Boon

indicators.note: against means placed next to, side by side
poor suggests the word in a bad state, its letters jumbled
a manoeuvre moves things about, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A Sioux military manoeuvre against poor Daniel Boone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' turns BOON into OBNO; 'manoeuvre' turns SIOUX into XIOUS; 'against' sets them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnoxious and offensive are synonyms for hateful or unpleasant.

clue.text: Backer's sort of horse is carrying a number in the race

definitions.note: backer's reads as backer is, a helper

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, of the horse family

indicators.note: in puts the article and number within the race

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

explanation.surface: A punter's horse is carrying a number in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorbike race; A N goes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer supports someone, as a helper or aide does.

clue.text: Glad eye, we hear, cast by her

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters are rearranged
we hear means a word said aloud stands for another sounding the same

parts.note: eye sounds like the letter I

explanation.surface: She gives a glad eye to the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns 'eye' into I, and 'cast' rearranges GLAD plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, famously Rita Hayworth's film role, so 'her' stands for it.

clue.text: Unusually early shoot begins, for birds

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd order, so the word is shuffled
begins picks the opening letter of shoot

explanation.surface: An unusually early shooting season opens for game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges EARLY to LAYER and 'begins' takes the first letter of 'shoot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens kept for egg production are called laying birds.

clue.text: Young beast takes early break for gin cocktail

indicators.note: break suggests the word broken up and its letters reordered
a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An animal takes an early break for a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges EARLY and 'cocktail' rearranges GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal in its second year, especially a racehorse, is called by this word.

clue.text: An untied knot — flood results!

indicators.note: knot suggests the letters tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An untied boat leads to a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knot' rearranges AN UNTIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to overwhelm with water, a synonym for swamping.

clue.text: Smash left minicar bent

indicators.note: smash means wreck, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Smash up a minicar left bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smash' rearranges MINICAR to CRIMINA, then L for left is added; 'bent' is slang for dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is slang for crooked or dishonest, which describes a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Cormorant heading for bay tree

parts.note: the shag is a species of cormorant
a dog's bay is its bark

explanation.surface: A cormorant heads for a bay tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A shag is a seabird of the cormorant family; 'bay' is a dog's bark, not the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American hickory with shaggy, peeling bark is a kind of tree.

clue.text: It signals to traveller turning up with fish, on key

indicators.note: turning up in a down light reads these words from bottom to top

parts.note: a rep is a travelling salesman

explanation.surface: A traveller turns up with fish on a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses REP and EEL together into LEEPER, set under B, the key.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager that beeps to summon its carrier is a device that signals.

clue.text: Beam swivelling in a circle pinpoints this parasite

indicators.note: in puts the circle inside the turned beam
swivelling suggests the letters turned about

parts.note: a circle is the letter O

explanation.surface: A swivelling beam pinpoints a parasite under the microscope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swivelling' rearranges BEAM to MEBA; 'in' puts O inside, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Some single-celled protozoa of this kind live as parasites, causing dysentery.

clue.text: From here view motorway with road winding to river

indicators.note: winding suggests a twisting path, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A view of the motorway with a road winding to a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written MI; 'winding' rearranges ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish turret or belvedere is a viewpoint from which to take in the scenery.

clue.text: We object to puckish character introducing new form of altruism

indicators.note: introducing means bringing a piece into the others

parts.note: the object form of we is us
Puck is a mischievous sprite, an elf

explanation.surface: We object to an impish sprite bringing in a new form of altruism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We object' means we in the object case, US; 'introducing' puts N into US plus ELF.
explanation.definitionFit: Selflessness, putting others first, is a form of altruism.

clue.text: Offer me shelter in a fight

explanation.surface: Someone offers shelter in the middle of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Lee is shelter from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused hand-to-hand scuffle is a kind of fight.

clue.text: Being thus pre-eminent, girl has right to stylishness in dress

explanation.surface: A pre-eminent girl has a right to style in dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a king or queen in being supreme in rank.

clue.text: Beater chasing red deer round the point

indicators.note: round means placed around the point

parts.note: a hart is a male red deer
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Beaters chase red deer round the point on a hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts E inside HART; 'Beater' is not a hunt beater.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ that pumps blood beats, so it is a beater.

clue.text: Pennine church rebuilt for a very modest sum

indicators.note: rebuilt means reconstructed in a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A Pennine church rebuilt for a tiny sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges PENNINE; the Pennines are hills in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine old pence was a small amount in pre-decimal British money.

clue.text: Duck an old sailor

explanation.surface: A duck that is an old sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A male duck shares its name with Sir Francis, the Elizabethan seafarer.

clue.text: Lop a fir tree severely to make it grow rapidly

indicators.note: severely suggests hacking the phrase about, rearranging it

explanation.surface: Lop a fir tree hard to make it grow back fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'severely' rearranges LOP A FIR TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To multiply quickly is to increase rapidly in number.
